topic: Non-exam course: Independent Critical Study - Texts Across Time
subject: english-literature

moments.title: A Room of One's Own
moments.body: 1929: Woolf's foundational essay argues that material conditions (income, private space) determine women's literary production. The fictional Judith Shakespeare — Shakespeare's equally talented sister — would have been driven to suicide by lack of education and opportunity.
moments.takeaway: Woolf's essay sat largely unrecognised as theory until second-wave feminism in the 1970s.

moments.title: Second-wave feminist criticism
moments.who: Kate Millett, Mary Ellmann, Elaine Showalter
moments.body: Millett's 'Sexual Politics' (1970), Ellmann's 'Thinking About Women' (1968), Showalter's 'A Literature of Their Own' (1977). The feminist project — recover women writers excluded from the canon, expose patriarchal assumptions in male-authored canonical texts.
moments.takeaway: Showalter's coinage 'gynocriticism' distinguished the recovery project from feminist critique of male texts.

moments.title: Gilbert and Gubar's Madwoman in the Attic
moments.body: 1979: 'The Madwoman in the Attic: The Woman Writer and the Nineteenth-Century Literary Imagination'. The argument: 19th-century women writers (Brontë, Eliot, Dickinson) constructed alternative figures — angels and madwomen — to express what patriarchal aesthetics denied them. The book is a foundational text of feminist criticism.
moments.takeaway: Gilbert and Gubar's 'anxiety of authorship' adapts Harold Bloom's 'anxiety of influence' for women writers.

now.title: Feminist criticism now
now.body: Feminist criticism is now woven into mainstream literary study. Intersectional approaches (Crenshaw, bell hooks, Audre Lorde) extended the feminist project to race, class, sexuality. Trans literary criticism, queer feminism, ecofeminism continue to develop the framework.
now.open_questions: Is feminist criticism still a separate field or fully integrated? Many feminist critics argue it should disappear once its concerns are fully absorbed; others see continuing structural patriarchy in publishing and curriculum.

reflection: Feminist literary criticism reshaped what counts as literature, what questions to ask of texts, and who the canon serves. Its impact — on syllabuses, anthologies, prize lists, criticism — has been one of the most consequential intellectual shifts in the discipline.
